findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so get_item_key receives an AuditLogEntry datetime, not a number. Calling math.floor or math.ceil on it raises TypeError when build_cursor processes any nonempty result set, making optimized audit-log requests fail with a server error. value_from_cursor also returns the raw numeric cursor rather than converting it to a datetime for the database predicate. Reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions for this endpoint.

findings.title: Django querysets do not support the advertised negative offsets
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset, this branch passes a negative slice start to a Django QuerySet. Django explicitly rejects negative indexing with ValueError; it does not handle these boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, the new negative-offset feature produces a server error instead of a page. Implement reverse traversal using supported nonnegative slices and ordering, or reject such cursors with a pagination validation error.

findings.title: Do not dereference an optional organization member on every request
findings.body: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member can be None for organization-scoped API-token requests, which do not represent an organization member. For a non-superuser request, this expression dereferences that missing member and raises AttributeError. Because enable_advanced is computed even when optimized_pagination is absent, this breaks previously supported ordinary audit-log requests as well as optimized ones. Guard against a missing member and only evaluate advanced eligibility when the optimized path is requested.
